The Welsh Rugby Union has joined a network of more than 700 Welsh employers to pledge support to the armed forces community.
WRU Chief Executive Officer Abi Tierney, Brigadier Mark Davis CBE and WRU President Terry Cobner with the Armed Forces Covenant signed at Cardiff Castle (L-R). Copyright: RFCA for Wales.
Terry Cobner, president of the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU), and Abi Tierney, Chief Executive Officer of the WRU, signed the Armed Forces Covenant (AFC), with Brigadier Mark Davis CBE, Commander of 160 th (Welsh) Brigade, Head of the Army in Wales.
The signing took place at Cardiff Castle on Tuesday 8 September 2026 where the WRU representatives were honoured guests at the 21 Gun Salute to celebrate Accession Day; the anniversary of His Majesty King Charles III’s accession to the throne.
They were treated to music from the Regimental Band and Corps of Drums of The 3 rd Battalion, The Royal Welsh. Lance Corporal Shenkin, the Regimental Goat of the 3 rd Battalion, The Royal Welsh, along with the Goat Major, Sergeant Mark Jackson, were also in attendance.
We are proud to support the armed forces community in this way. Welsh rugby has a long and positive association with the 3 rd Battalion The Royal Welsh in particular, with Shenkin the Regimental Goat an important fixture as our official mascot on match days at the Principality Stadium and the Regimental Band also a regular feature. Those who serve or have served in the UK armed forces and their families are always welcome in Welsh rugby.
Brigadier Mark Davis CBE, Commander of the Army in Wales and Vice-Chair of the Army Rugby Union, said:
Rugby is the Army’s game. It demanded courage under pressure, discipline, respect and an unshakeable commitment to the team. These values are shared by Welsh rugby and our armed forces, reflecting a relationship forged over generations. By signing the AFC, the WRU is putting those values into action and standing with our whole armed forces community.
The AFC is a promise from the nation that those who serve or have served in the UK armed forces, and their families, are treated fairly. The programme in Wales is delivered by the Reserve Forces’ and Cadets’ Association for Wales’ Defence Relationship Managers on behalf of the Ministry of Defence (MOD).
Throughout the UK some 13,000 organisations have signed up to the AFC including a growing number in Wales.
The 21 Gun Salute was delivered by reservists from 104 Regiment Royal Artillery who are among 1,400 reservists serving in Wales. They are people who come from diverse backgrounds and give up their spare time to train and serve alongside regular personnel in the armed forces.
Mr Craig Middle, the MOD’s Defence Relationship Manager for South Wales, said:
We are delighted that the WRU has shown its support to the armed forces community. The number of organisations signing the Covenant is continuing to grow at an encouraging rate in Wales and indicates a positive outlook for the armed forces community.
